name: obrotomierz-open-data
description: Read-only open data from obrotomierz.pl: Polish retail treasury savings bonds, retail government bonds in 195 countries and account opening bonus data for banks in the 27 EU countries. CC BY 4.0.

interface.longDescription:
Read-only access to three open datasets published by obrotomierz.pl, a Polish website about safe savings. No sign-in.

Polish retail treasury savings bonds (OTS, ROR, DOR, TOS, COI, EDO, ROS, ROD): the current offer, and any series since 1999 by its code, with the margin, early redemption fee and the interest rate in every period that has started.

Retail government bonds in 195 countries (UN members, the Holy See and Palestine) and Hong Kong: whether a country sells government bonds to individuals at issue and how they pay (inflation plus a fixed margin, market real rate, fixed, floating, step-up or prize), with an official source for each country.

Banks in the 27 EU countries that pay a cash bonus for opening a personal current account, read one by one from bank websites, with the amount, deadline and source page.

Every answer names its source, the CC BY 4.0 license and the dataset DOI in Zenodo. Intended for people comparing safe savings options and for researchers and journalists. Limitations: the data is information, not financial advice; bank terms change often, so the binding terms are always on the bank or issuer page. The plugin cannot buy bonds, open accounts or access any user account.
defaultPrompt: Which Polish savings bonds are on sale now?
Which countries sell inflation-linked savings bonds to individuals?
Which banks in Spain pay a bonus for opening an account?

positive.description: Current offer of Polish savings bonds
positive.prompt: Which Polish savings bonds are on sale now and what do they pay in the first period?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the series on sale this month (for example COI, DOR, EDO) with term, first-period rate, margin over inflation where relevant, early redemption fee and the source.

positive.prompt: Show the interest periods of the Polish bond series EDO1126.
positive.expected_behavior: Returns EDO1126 (sold from November 2016): 120-month term, margin over inflation, early redemption fee and the rate of each of its 10 interest periods, with the source.

positive.prompt: Does Hungary sell inflation-linked government bonds to individuals?
positive.expected_behavior: Says yes: Hungary sells PMÁP (inflation plus a fixed margin) and other retail bonds, with the official source link.

positive.description: Countries with inflation plus a fixed margin
positive.prompt: Which countries sell inflation-linked savings bonds with a fixed margin to ordinary people?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns the count per category and names the six countries paying inflation plus a margin fixed at purchase (Czechia, Hungary, Italy, Poland, South Africa, United States).

positive.description: Account opening bonuses in one EU country
positive.prompt: Which banks in Spain pay a bonus for opening a personal account?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the Spanish banks with a cash bonus in the dataset (amount in EUR, deadline, source page) and notes that binding terms are on the bank page.

negative.prompt: Buy ten EDO bonds for me.
Open an account at Banco Santander for me and claim the bonus.
Should I put all my savings into EDO bonds?

review.commerce_description: The plugin only reads open data. It does not sell anything or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: four read-only tools over three open datasets (Polish savings bonds, retail government bonds by country, EU account opening bonuses).
